notes: kb/Work PB5702: COBOL 2002 is judged by its own Annex C.2 (TR 10176:2001) and folded by its own Annex D. a) every character of C.2.1 and C.2.2 is an extended letter of the UTF-16 compile-time set (the 2002 repertoire is a subset of the 2014 or 2023 tables, AnnexBCDriftTests). b) the special characters of C.2.1 (U+00B5, U+0559, U+2102 ...) and C.2.2's MIDDLE DOT, and the combining characters (the rows 2014's Annex B.3.1 labels combining, within the 2002 repertoire, because 2002 Annex C labels none), are the medial class: COBOL2773 first or last, accepted inside a word; a character outside Annex C.2 (Syriac, Thaana, Sinhala ...) is COBOL2773. Witnesses at --std 2002: pb5702 accepted test (X, micro sign, y and L, middle dot, L accepted; output ONE TWO) and the refused pb5702 last-in-a-word test (COBOL2773 for Xmicro). c) GR4c: CobolNames.D2002Mappings transcribes 2002 Annex D.2.1 and D.2.2 (600 pairs, less the two that cross between a basic and an extended letter); CobolNames.Fold(cp, 2002) reads it and EditionSpelling writes each character the 2002 table folds differently from 2023's in the 2002 key, or, where 2002 leaves a character alone that 2023 folds (U+2160), as a stand-in no word may hold, so X(U+2160)Y and X(U+2170)Y are two items at --std 2002 and one name at 2014 and 2023; Annex D prints (0256,0189) beside (0189,0256), so U+0189 and U+0256 are two letters at 2002. d) (combining characters count separately in a word's length) is not witnessed by this change, and GR3 above covers only the basic letters.
